For a `map[string]string` it stores the **last** value: `ptrMap[k] = v[len(v)-1]` (line 399, with the comment `// pick last`). So for a form key with multiple values it keeps the final one, discarding the earlier ones. (For `map[string][]string` it copies the whole slice of values.)

With an empty string and no `test.v` flag, `SetMode("")` falls back to `DebugMode` (`value = DebugMode`), then sets `ginMode = debugCode` and `modeName = DebugMode`. So gin stays in debug mode (it does not panic and does not switch to test mode).

Fixed (#4). In `response_writer.go`, `WriteHeader` was recording the new status code even when the header had already been flushed to the client, so `c.Writer.Status()` could report a code the client never received. Added an early `return` after the "Headers were already written" warning so the recorded status is no longer overridden once written (matching net/http's behaviour of ignoring superfluous WriteHeader calls). Verified: full `go test ./...` passes, `go vet` clean, no pre-existing test broken, temp probe files removed.

It falls through the switch and returns `false, ErrMultiFileHeader` — i.e. `isSet = false` and the error `errors.New("unsupported field type for multipart.FileHeader")` (the last line of the function, line 60).

Fixed (#1). In `errors.go`, `Error.Error()` is on a value receiver, so a value `gin.Error` implemented `error`, but `Unwrap()` was on a pointer receiver, so value `gin.Error` did not satisfy `interface{ Unwrap() error }` — `errors.Is`/`errors.As`/`errors.Unwrap` failed for the value form (contradicting Unwrap's own docstring). Changed `func (msg *Error) Unwrap() error` to `func (msg Error) Unwrap() error` (errors.go:94). Both `Error` and `*Error` now unwrap. Verified with a temporary probe test (pointer form, value form, errors.As to *Error, direct errors.Unwrap) plus an out-of-package check; full `go test ./...` passes, `go vet` clean, no pre-existing test broken, temp files removed.

It aborts the request and writes a 500 status:

```go
func defaultHandleRecovery(c *Context, err any) {
	c.AbortWithStatus(http.StatusInternalServerError)
}
```

`AbortWithStatus` sets the status code to 500, writes the header, and calls `c.Abort()` so no further handlers run. It is the default handler used by `Recovery()`/`RecoveryWithWriter` when no custom `RecoveryFunc` is supplied.

It falls back to `time.RFC3339` (`"2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00"`):

```go
timeFormat := structField.Tag.Get("time_format")
if timeFormat == "" {
	timeFormat = time.RFC3339
}
```

The value is then parsed with `time.ParseInLocation(timeFormat, val, l)`, where the location comes from `time_utc` / `time_location` tags (defaulting to `time.Local`). (Note the special formats `unix` and `unixNano` are handled separately, before this.)

Fixed (#18). `Context.FileAttachment` interpolated the filename raw into the quoted Content-Disposition value, so a filename containing `"` or `\` produced a broken/injectable header. Added a `quoteEscaper` replacer (same approach as mime/multipart) and escaped the ASCII filename: `attachment; filename="new\"filename.go"` now round-trips through mime.ParseMediaType. The UTF-8 branch (filename*=UTF-8''...) is unchanged. Verified: all existing attachment tests pass, full suite green, go vet clean, temp probe files removed.
